subtopic: Binary Search and Monotonic Search Spaces
question_text: When implementing binary search on a monotonically increasing array to find the first occurrence of an element, which boundary update prevents infinite looping when `left + 1 == right`?

options.text: mid = left + (right - left) // 2 and left = mid + 1
mid = left + (right - left) // 2 and right = mid
mid = left + (right - left) // 2 and left = mid

answer_explanation: When searching for the first occurrence with an open/closed boundary invariant, choosing `mid = left + (right - left) // 2` truncates towards left. Setting `right = mid` safely preserves candidate first matches without infinite looping.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: When searching for the first occurrence with an open/closed boundary invariant, choosing `mid = left + (right - left) // 2` truncates towards left. Setting `right = mid` safely preserves candidate first matches without infinite looping.
